Phoenix / Week's cooling.note: Phoenix gains the most from Passive House: about half the cooling of the code house, in every climate.
Phoenix / Week's cooling.axis: Wh per m² of floor, over the week

Phoenix / Peak cooling.note: The peak grows far less than the week: 6 to 7% by 2080 in Phoenix. Passive House cuts it by more than a third.
Phoenix / Peak cooling.axis: W per m² of floor, in the peak hour

Phoenix / Hours too hot.note: Phoenix looks the safest of the four: neither house passes a heat index of 32 °C until 2080. How much of that is Phoenix, and how much the model of the ground, is taken up below.
Phoenix / Hours too hot.axis: Hours over a heat index of 32 °C, of the 128 without power

Austin / Week's cooling.note: In Austin, Passive House saves about a third, and both houses need over 40% more cooling by 2080.
Austin / Week's cooling.axis: Wh per m² of floor, over the week

Austin / Peak cooling.note: Austin's peak grows by 8% by 2080, in both houses. Passive House cuts it by a quarter.
Austin / Peak cooling.axis: W per m² of floor, in the peak hour

Austin / Hours too hot.note: In Austin the two houses are alike until 2050. After that the Passive House has about a fifth fewer hours over a heat index of 32 °C.
Austin / Hours too hot.axis: Hours over a heat index of 32 °C, of the 128 without power

Miami / Week's cooling.note: Miami needs the most cooling of the four. Passive House saves a third of it, in every climate.
Miami / Week's cooling.axis: Wh per m² of floor, over the week

Miami / Peak cooling.note: Miami has the highest peak. Passive House cuts it by 35 to 41%, and it grows by 7 to 15% by 2080.
Miami / Peak cooling.axis: W per m² of floor, in the peak hour

Miami / Hours too hot.note: In Miami the airtight Passive House has far fewer hours over a heat index of 32 °C: 14 against 48 now, 60 against 96 by 2080.
Miami / Hours too hot.axis: Hours over a heat index of 32 °C, of the 128 without power

DC / Week's cooling.note: DC saves the least from Passive House, 15 to 18%. Both houses need 36 to 41% more cooling by 2080.
DC / Week's cooling.axis: Wh per m² of floor, over the week

DC / Peak cooling.note: DC's Passive House peak grows the most of any, 20% by 2080, but is still 13% under the code house.
DC / Peak cooling.axis: W per m² of floor, in the peak hour

DC / Hours too hot.note: In DC the Passive House is worse than the code house: its insulated slab cuts it off from the cool of the ground.
DC / Hours too hot.axis: Hours over a heat index of 32 °C, of the 128 without power
